assumptions: Quantities are planned for four people so the plan also covers weeks when only three people eat; surplus becomes a planned lunch.
Check existing stock before shopping, especially essentials, seasonings, spreads, frozen food, and household goods.
Fresh fish, lettuce, berries, and opened cold meats are used early; robust vegetables, frozen foods, and store-cupboard meals are used later.
The supplied mealplan_schema.json file was empty, so this uses a clear best-effort structure and could not be validated against the intended schema.

breakfast.meal: Box of Cereal with Soy Milk
breakfast.notes: Open the soy milk and cereal at the start of the week; measure portions rather than free-pouring to make one standard box last.

lunch.notes: Use the opened seeded loaf and ham early. Freeze half the loaf immediately if it will not be used within three days.

dinner.notes: Fresh salmon is the most time-sensitive dinner, so it is scheduled first. Buy one four-fillet pack, or two two-fillet packs if that is the standard size. Roast the whole broccoli stalk after slicing it thinly to avoid waste.

breakfast.notes: Uses the same opened soy milk as Monday. Add a few blueberries before the soft fruit deteriorates.

lunch.meal: Leek and Potato Soup with Bread
lunch.notes: Make four portions using potatoes shared with Monday and Thursday dinners. Use the green leek tops in the soup rather than discarding them.

dinner.notes: Use lettuce while crisp and two of the pepper multipack. Cook about 600 g chicken; reserve roughly 150 g cooked filling for Wednesday lunch before serving.

breakfast.meal: Toast with Peanut Butter or Jam
breakfast.notes: Finish the first loaf or use slices frozen on Monday. Peanut butter adds protein and is longer-lasting than opening another chilled item.

lunch.notes: Use the reserved cooked fajita chicken and remaining wraps. Keep the chicken chilled and use within one day.

dinner.notes: Roast a 1.8-2.0 kg chicken with potatoes and carrots. Strip the carcass after dinner: chill enough meat for Thursday lunch and dinner, and freeze any further surplus. The carcass can be frozen for stock.

breakfast.notes: Use self-raising flour, eggs, and soy milk already bought for the week. Freeze spare pancakes individually for a quick breakfast.

lunch.notes: First use of Wednesday's roast chicken leftovers. Add any sound leftover lettuce from fajitas.

dinner.notes: Finishes the chilled roast chicken and remaining fresh peppers and onion. Frozen sweetcorn avoids opening another perishable pack. Reheat chicken until piping hot and only once.

breakfast.meal: Box of Cereal with Soy Milk
breakfast.notes: Finish the first opened soy milk carton; open the second only if needed.

lunch.notes: A store-cupboard lunch suits later in the week. Four tins provide one tin per person; use two rice pouches if each pouch serves two.

dinner.meal: Beef Chilli with Rice and Kidney Beans
dinner.notes: Cook six portions from a 500 g mince pack, tomatoes, kidney beans, carrot, celery, and onion. Serve four and chill two promptly for Saturday lunch, eliminating half-used packs.

breakfast.notes: Top with raisins or sliced banana to use fruit already in the snack allocation.

lunch.notes: Planned for two adults from Friday's batch; supplement remaining diners with beans or spaghetti on toast. Reheat the chilli until piping hot.

dinner.notes: Frozen ingredients and tins are deliberately used near the end of the week because they will not spoil if plans change. Cook only the number of fish fingers and chips required.

breakfast.meal: Toast with Marmalade or Peanut Butter
breakfast.notes: Use bread from the freezer and long-life spreads, preventing a second loaf from going stale.

lunch.notes: A flexible store-cupboard lunch that uses the remaining bread. Open only the number of tins needed for the people eating.

dinner.notes: Frozen sausages and peas are saved for the final day. Use the remaining potatoes and make only enough mash for the diners present.

waste_reduction_summary: Use salmon, ham, lettuce, blueberries, grapes, and chilled yoghurt in the first half of the week.
Turn Tuesday's fajita chicken into Wednesday lunch and Wednesday's roast chicken into both Thursday meals.
Cook six chilli portions on Friday so two portions become Saturday lunch.
Split full packs across meals: peppers across fajitas and stir fry, potatoes across four meals, and bread across breakfasts and lunches.
Freeze bread on purchase, freeze unused celery for a future sauce or soup, and keep the final dinners largely frozen or shelf-stable.
